===  chart.py
import plotly.graph_objects as go

data = {
    'Year': [2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019],
    'Maritime Shipping': [14.5, 15.2, 15.8, 16.2, 16.8, 17.3, 17.9, 18.4, 19.0, 19.6],
    'Air Cargo Logistics': [18.9, 19.3, 19.8, 20.3, 20.9, 21.4, 22.0, 22.6, 23.2, 23.8],
    'Heavy Road Freight': [8.3, 8.5, 8.7, 9.1, 9.4, 9.6, 9.9, 10.2, 10.5, 10.8],
    'Domestic Passenger Air': [12.1, 12.5, 12.9, 13.4, 13.9, 14.3, 14.8, 15.2, 15.6, 16.0],
    'International Passenger Air': [10.2, 10.8, 11.1, 11.5, 11.9, 12.3, 12.8, 13.2, 13.7, 14.1],
    'Oil Pipeline Transport': [9.1, 9.4, 9.6, 10.0, 10.3, 10.7, 11.0, 11.3, 11.6, 12.0]
}

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=data['Year'],
    y=data['Maritime Shipping'],
    mode='lines',
    name='Maritime Shipping',
    stackgroup='one',
    line=dict(width=0.5, color='#d62728')
))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=data['Year'],
    y=data['Air Cargo Logistics'],
    mode='lines',
    name='Air Cargo Logistics',
    stackgroup='one',
    line=dict(width=0.5, color='#ff7f0e')
))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=data['Year'],
    y=data['Heavy Road Freight'],
    mode='lines',
    name='Heavy Road Freight',
    stackgroup='one',
    line=dict(width=0.5, color='#2ca02c')
))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=data['Year'],
    y=data['Domestic Passenger Air'],
    mode='lines',
    name='Domestic Passenger Air',
    stackgroup='one',
    line=dict(width=0.5, color='#1f77b4')
))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=data['Year'],
    y=data['International Passenger Air'],
    mode='lines',
    name='International Passenger Air',
    stackgroup='one',
    line=dict(width=0.5, color='#9467bd')
))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=data['Year'],
    y=data['Oil Pipeline Transport'],
    mode='lines',
    name='Oil Pipeline Transport',
    stackgroup='one',
    line=dict(width=0.5, color='#8c564b')
))

fig.update_layout(
    title='Annual Economic Impact of Transportation Sectors in Lebanon (2010-2019)',
    xaxis_title='Year',
    yaxis_title='Annual Transportation Volume (Million Tonnes)',
    showlegend=True,
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1),
    hovermode="x unified",
    plot_bgcolor='white',
    height=600,
    width=1000,
    margin=dict(l=50, r=50, b=50, t=80, pad=4)
)

fig.write_image('output.png')
===  summary.txt
The image is an area chart illustrating the annual economic impact of various transportation sectors in Lebanon from 2010 to 2019. The chart features a stacked design, where each sector's contribution is layered on top of the others, allowing for a cumulative view of their combined economic impact over time. The x-axis represents the years from 2010 to 2019, while the y-axis measures the annual economic impact in billion USD, ranging from 0 to 100 billion.

The chart includes six distinct transportation sectors, each represented by a different color. Maritime Shipping, shown in blue, consistently contributes the largest economic impact, starting at approximately 14.5 billion USD in 2010 and gradually increasing to around 19.6 billion USD by 2019. The next layer, depicted in light brown, represents International Passenger Air, which begins at about 18.9 billion USD in 2010 and rises to around 23.8 billion USD by 2019. Domestic Passenger Air, illustrated in red, starts at 12.1 billion USD in 2010 and grows to roughly 16.0 billion USD by 2019.

Air Cargo Logistics, shown in orange, begins at 10.2 billion USD in 2010 and increases to 14.1 billion USD in 2019. The green area represents Heavy Road Freight, which starts at 8.3 billion USD in 2010 and grows to 10.8 billion USD by 2019. Finally, Oil Pipeline Transport, depicted in a muted brown, starts at 9.1 billion USD in 2010 and rises to 12.0 billion USD in 2019. The cumulative economic impact of all sectors combined reaches nearly 100 billion USD by 2019, demonstrating steady growth across the decade. The chart's title and legend at the top provide clear context and identification for each sector.

args.message:
I fixed the three diagnosed flaws in chart.py and re-ran it to regenerate output.png:
1. **Swapped series:** Air Cargo Logistics and International Passenger Air had each other's data. They now match table.csv (Air Cargo 10.2→14.1, International Passenger Air 18.9→23.8).
2. **Color:** Maritime Shipping was red, but the summary says blue. I swapped its color with Domestic Passenger Air, so Maritime is now `#1f77b4` (blue) and Domestic is `#d62728` (red), matching the summary.
3. **Y-axis label:** it now reads "Annual Economic Impact (Billion USD)" instead of the transport-volume label.

**Verified on the figure object:** every trace's name, color and first/last values match the table and summary, and the y-axis title is the new text. The rendered y-axis runs 0–100, as the summary describes.

**Left as is:**
- International Passenger Air stays purple even though the summary says "light brown", because only one color was flagged as wrong.
- The legend overlaps the title, as the rendered output.png shows. The legend placement and margins in chart.py are unchanged from the original, so I left the layout alone rather than restyle something outside the three listed flaws.
